caveats: 6 unexpected errors across 64400 timed operations of the sweep (N=2: 1 at 100 writers; N=5: 1 at 50 and 3 at 100; N=10: 1 at 100). Do not report the sweep as error-free.
'contribute' is a no-op in this harness and still counts in the throughput denominator (2 of every 20 timed operations).
Single host, 16 cores, no WAN latency: site containers share one machine's CPU and page cache, so this measures process-level separation, not geographic distribution.
Not comparable to experiments/35_v28_concurrency, which measures in-process SQLAlchemy service calls under a uniform six-operation mix.
N=1 is a degenerate topology retained as the sweep's baseline, not a supported deployment.

config.compose: regenerated per N by generate_compose.py; containers torn down with volumes between topologies
config.operation_mix: _MIX_REALISTIC, 20 entries: query x8, commit x7, contribute x2, attest x1, dispute x1, restore x1
config.storage: direct sqlite3 inside each container; no audit-history table

findings.low_load_cost: At one writer, ten sites are 20.6% slower than one (99.83 vs 125.67 ops/s): dispute and restore fan out synchronously to every site.
findings.note: The whole gain is realized at N=2; N=5 and N=10 do not improve on it. The shared evidence service, contacted by every site for attest/dispute/restore, is the remaining bottleneck.

label: v33_equal_stack_site_count
purpose: Isolate the contribution of distribution itself. Stack, transport, operation mix, worker counts, ops-per-worker, warm-up and repeat count are all held fixed; DIB_DIST_N_SITES is the single independent variable. This is the equal-stack comparison that the withdrawn single-node-vs-distributed throughput ratio could not provide.
